$$\text{Sum} = (n - 2) \times 180°$$
For a hexagon, $n = 6$:
$$(6 - 2) \times 180° = 4 \times 180° = 720°$$
Every hexagon's interior angles must add up to exactly $720°$.

$$720° - 580° = 140°$$

Two straight lines crossing at $A$ form two pairs of **vertical angles**. The angles inside our two triangles at $A$ are $\angle BAC$ and $\angle EAD$ — they are vertical angles, so:
$$\angle BAC \cong \angle EAD$$
steps.title: Identify Vertical Angles at A

steps.description:
Matching up $\triangle ABC$ with $\triangle AED$ vertex-by-vertex ($A \leftrightarrow A$, $B \leftrightarrow E$, $C \leftrightarrow D$), we now have **two angles and a non-included side**:

| Part | $\triangle ABC$ | $\triangle AED$ | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| Angle | $\angle ABC$ | $\angle AED$ | Given |
| Angle | $\angle BAC$ | $\angle EAD$ | Vertical angles |
| Side (non-included) | $\overline{AC}$ | $\overline{AE}$ | Given |

By **AAS** (Angle-Angle-Side), two angles and the side not between them are congruent in both triangles, so $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle AED$. $\blacksquare$

steps.description:
For any polygon with $n$ sides, the interior angles always sum to $(n-2) \times 180°$. This formula comes from the fact that any polygon can be split into $(n-2)$ triangles, each contributing $180°$.

For a hexagon, $n = 6$:
$$(6 - 2) \times 180° = 4 \times 180° = 720°$$

Every hexagon's interior angles must add up to exactly $720°$.

meta.prompt: You are a worldclass math professor with expertise in breaking down math problem || Problem: $\triangle ABC$ has a right angle at $C$, with $AB = 13$ and $AC = 5$. Find $BC$. Then find the area of $\t

steps.description:
We have a right triangle with the right angle at $C$, so the two **legs** are $AC = 5$ and $BC$ (unknown), and the **hypotenuse** is $AB = 13$.

The Pythagorean theorem says: for any right triangle, $$\text{leg}_1^2 + \text{leg}_2^2 = \text{hypotenuse}^2$$

We know the hypotenuse and one leg, so we can solve for the other leg by **subtracting** the known leg² from the hypotenuse².
steps.title: Understand the Setup

steps.description:
Plug the known values into $AC^2 + BC^2 = AB^2$:
$$5^2 + BC^2 = 13^2$$
$$25 + BC^2 = 169$$
$$BC^2 = 144$$
$$BC = \sqrt{144} = 12$$

**Shortcut to notice:** $5$-$12$-$13$ is a well-known **Pythagorean triple** — a family of whole-number solutions to the Pythagorean theorem. Recognizing it lets you skip the arithmetic entirely.
steps.title: Find BC with Pythagorean Theorem

steps.description:
The area of a triangle is $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$. The two **legs** of a right triangle are always perpendicular to each other, making them the perfect base and height pair — no extra work needed.
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AC \times BC = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 30$$
steps.title: Find the Area

steps.description:
We're given that every **exterior angle** of a regular polygon is $24°$, and we need to find the number of sides and each interior angle.

The key insight: **all exterior angles of any polygon, regardless of the number of sides, always add up to exactly $360°$**. Think of it like walking around the entire polygon — you make one full turn, which is $360°$. Since the polygon is **regular**, every exterior angle is equal, so we can simply divide $360°$ by the size of one exterior angle to count how many sides there are.
steps.title: Understand the Problem

steps.description:
Dividing the total $360°$ by each exterior angle gives the number of sides:
$$n = \frac{360°}{24°} = 15$$
The polygon has **15 sides** (called a **pentadecagon**).
steps.title: Find the Number of Sides

steps.description:
An interior angle and its exterior angle sit on a straight line, so they are **supplementary** — they always add up to $180°$.
$$\text{Interior angle} = 180° - 24° = 156°$$
steps.title: Find Each Interior Angle

steps.description: We have an external point with two tangent segments drawn to a circle. The key geometric fact here is that **two tangent segments drawn from the same external point are always equal in length** — this is the Tangent-Tangent theorem. So all we need to do is set the two expressions equal and solve for $x$.
steps.title: Understand the Problem

steps.description:
Since both tangent segments have the same length:
$$3x - 4 = x + 10$$
steps.title: Set Expressions Equal

steps.description:
Subtract $x$ from both sides:
$$2x - 4 = 10$$
Add $4$ to both sides:
$$2x = 14$$
Divide by $2$:
$$x = 7$$
steps.title: Solve for $x$

steps.description:
Substitute $x = 7$ into either expression (both must give the same result):
$$3(7) - 4 = 21 - 4 = 17$$
$$7 + 10 = 17 ✓$$
Both segments equal $17$.
steps.title: Find the Length
